question.text:
The median nerve lies immediately ulnar to which of the following structures at the level of the distal radioulnar joint?
Answer Choices: (A) Flexor digitorum profundus (B) Flexor carpi ulnaris (C) Flexor digitorum superficialis (D) Brachioradialis (E) Pronator teres (F) Extensor carpi radialis longus (G) Palmaris longus (H) Flexor pollicis longus (I) Radial artery (J) Flexor carpi radialis

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The median nerve is located in the forearm, specifically at the wrist. The ulnar nerve is located on the ulnar side of the forearm. The question asks which structure lies immediately ulnar to the median nerve at the distal radioulnar joint. The flexor carpi ulnaris is the primary flexor of the wrist on the ulnar side. The other options are located on the radial side of the forearm.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The median nerve is located on the palmar side of the wrist, and the flexor carpi ulnaris is the primary flexor on the ulnar side.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: Flexor digitorum profundus is on the palmar side, but not immediately ulnar to the median nerve. Brachioradialis is proximal to the distal radioulnar joint. Pronator teres is in the anterior compartment of the forearm. Extensor carpi radialis longus is on the radial side. Palmaris longus is on the palmar side. Flexor pollicis longus is on the palmar side. Radial artery is on the radial side. Flexor carpi radialis is on the radial side.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The median nerve is located on the ulnar side of the wrist. At the distal radioulnar joint, it lies immediately ulnar to the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle, which is the most superficial flexor of the wrist on the ulnar side. This anatomical relationship is consistent with the nerve's course and the muscle's position.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The median nerve's course along the ulnar side of the wrist and its relationship with the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: Other muscles on the ulnar side (like flexor carpi radialis) are more superficial or located on different sides, and the radial artery is a vascular structure not relevant to this question

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: At the level of the distal radioulnar joint, the median nerve runs immediately ulnar to the flexor carpi ulnaris, which is a key anatomical landmark. The median nerve is located anteriorly and ulnar to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, which is part of the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle. This relationship is consistent across standard anatomical references and is critical for surgical and diagnostic planning in the wrist and forearm.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Anatomical dissection and cadaveric studies consistently show the median nerve lies ulnar to the flexor carpi ulnaris at the distal radioulnar joint.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Other options like flexor digitorum superficialis, palmaris longus, or radial artery are either more lateral or not adjacent in the same plane; brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus are more lateral and posterior; pronator teres is proximal; flexor pollicis longus is deeper and more medial. None match the precise anatomical relationship described.

openbio_8b.clinical_reasoning: The median nerve lies immediately ulnar to the Flexor carpi ulnaris at the level of the distal radioulnar joint.
